text:
priya: Heads up — ran a focused PCIe vs SXM set for the new quantized bring-up (redwood-rlhf-13b, 4-bit, per-channel) across us-west and eu-west. High-level: SXM wins for tail latency at long seqs due to NVLink KV-cache sharing, but PCIe nodes still have comparable steady-state throughput for small seqs. Details + numbers below.

priya: Quick test matrix: model=redwood-rlhf-13b-q4, batch={1,8}, seq={32,512}, topo={pcie,sxm}, region={us-west,eu-west}, kernels=auto vs cuda-graph+cuBLASLt+flash-attn.

priya: Paste of selected numbers (p50/p95 latency in ms, tokens/s throughput):
```
seq,Batch,Topo,Region,p50,p95,toks_s
32,1,pcie,us-west,12,18,7200
32,1,sxm,us-west,10,15,7400
512,1,pcie,us-west,95,215,420
512,1,sxm,us-west,68,120,520
512,8,pcie,us-west,480,1300,3200
512,8,sxm,us-west,360,700,4200
512,1,pcie,eu-west,110,260,390
512,1,sxm,eu-west,75,140,505
```

priya: Observations: 1) At seq=32 the gap is small (cache/KV not a big factor). 2) At seq=512 p95 on PCIe balloons — NVLink helps keep KV cache hops cheap on SXM. 3) Batch=8 throughput on SXM is ~30% higher for long contexts. 4) eu-west had slightly worse p95 on PCIe — suspected noisy neighbor and numa/layout defaults.

tom: Did you pin threads / do numa-bind? On PCIe boxes if kernel picks different cuda devices you get cross-socket traffic. Try: `numactl --physcpubind=+0-23 --membind=0 <cmd>` or `taskset` for the process.

ashley: Re: kernels — saw env fallback to a naive matmul on some PCIe machines when sequence>384. The runtime kernel selector seems to pick a precompiled kernel set. If it can't match compiled profiles it falls back. You can force libcublasLt/flash-attn combo with `INFER_KERNEL_HINT=cuBLASLt,flash` which helped p95 on some nodes.

lee: Also watch quantization layout. Per-channel 4-bit produces denser compute but increases reduction pressure during KV builds; that exacerbates PCIe inter-GPU shuffle costs. 8-bit qint felt marginally worse latency for small batches but smoother across p95.

tom: Can you share the exact runtime flags and how you measured KV transfer? I want to reproduce the cross-socket penalty.

priya: Runtime command snippet we used (CI bench harness):
```
./bench_infer.sh --model redwood-rlhf-13b-q4 \
  --backend redwood-runtime --batch 1 --seq 512 \
  --topo pcie --kernel auto --repeat 300 \
  > /tmp/bench/1819004321-pcie-512.log
```
KV microbench (measured total inter-GPU KV copy bandwidth):
```
pcie: ~3.2 GB/s (cross-socket pinned path)
sxm: 11.8 GB/s (nvlink bonded)
```

ashley: That matches what I saw. On PCIe the kernel selector sometimes inserts a memcpy-based KV sync instead of NVLink-aware transfer. I'll open a runtime flag to prefer NVLink-aware path (WIP: `FORCE_NVLINK_PATH=1`).

perf-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/bench/1819004321.tar.gz (contains logs, flamegraphs, csvs) :mag:

lee: Region note — eu-west PCIe hosts showed higher variance (p95 up by ~30-40ms) even when pinned. Suspect noisy host scheduling. You might want to retest on Dedicated capacity to confirm hardware-only behavior.

priya: Action items: 1) @ashley add `INFER_KERNEL_HINT` and `FORCE_NVLINK_PATH` toggles to runtime (low risk flag) — ticket assigned to you. 2) @tom reproduce numa-bind diff and post command + p95 delta. 3) I'll schedule a follow-up run on Dedicated and dump a perf profile.

priya: TL;DR — SXM/NVLink consistently reduces p95 for long contexts by ~25-40% and increases batch throughput ~20-35% for 13B q4 workloads. PCIe still OK for short contexts; ensure NUMA pinning and aggressive kernel matching to avoid memcpy fallbacks. :thumbsup:
